Review.ItemLabel: CrossOrgUserAdmin sees three tabs, not five
Review.HumanAction: Sign out and sign in as asmith@acmecoffee.com (seeded CrossOrgUserAdmin — user id 3 in user-roles.json). Navigate to /admin/security.
Review.Expectation: Only three tabs render: Organization Master Details, Users and Role Assignment, Role Documentation. Role Master Details and Default Masks are absent (compiled privileges forbid them).
Review.Feedback: Avery Smith can't see the security Tab at all.

Review.ItemLabel: BackofficeUser (plain user-type role) sees only Role Documentation
Review.HumanAction: Sign out and sign in as jdoe@acmecoffee.com (seeded BackofficeUser — user id 2). Navigate to /admin/security directly via URL.
Review.Expectation: Only the Role Documentation tab renders. All four administrative tabs are absent. No 403 page — the tab-gating is a visibility restriction, not a page restriction, for the Role Documentation path.
Review.Feedback: jdoe@acmecoffee.com does not see the Security tab at all.

Review.ItemLabel: Arrow keys move between tabs; Home/End jump to endpoints
Review.HumanAction: Signed in as SystemAdmin, click the Role Master Details tab to focus the tab strip. Press ArrowRight four times; observe each tab becoming active in order. Press ArrowLeft twice. Press Home; then press End.
Review.Expectation: ArrowRight advances one tab at a time and wraps from the last tab back to the first. ArrowLeft moves backward and wraps from the first tab to the last. Home activates Role Master Details. End activates Role Documentation. No layout shift or focus loss.

Review.ItemLabel: Open feedback for Shell and Access
Review.HumanAction: Use this row for any unscripted feedback about reaching the dashboard or per-role tab gating.

Review.ItemLabel: All roles appear with baked-in rows greyed and chipped
Review.HumanAction: Signed in as SystemAdmin, open the Role Master Details tab. Review the grid.
Review.Expectation: Every role is listed: SystemAdmin, CrossOrgUserAdmin, CrossOrgMonitor, UserAdmin, User (all greyed with a 'baked-in' chip), plus user-type roles BackofficeUser, WarehouseUser, and Customer (not greyed). A FilterPanel<T> appears above the grid with fields for canonical name, alias, and description.
Review.Feedback: The Display alias column cuts off the Display alias text, and the font is larger than that of the other columns.  It would be nice to be able to adjust the column width to see the content.  That said, why can't the column widths dynamically adjust like the column widths for HTML tables.  And perhaps there should be text wrapping.

Review.ItemLabel: Filter panel narrows the grid by alias
Review.HumanAction: In the FilterPanel, add a filter on Alias contains 'Warehouse'. Apply.
Review.Expectation: Only the WarehouseUser row remains in the grid. Clearing the filter restores all rows.

Review.ItemLabel: DisplayAlias is inline-editable for both baked-in and user-type rows
Review.HumanAction: Click the DisplayAlias cell for SystemAdmin (a baked-in row). Change it to 'Platform Owner'. Press Tab or click outside. Then click the DisplayAlias cell for BackofficeUser and change it to 'Back Office Staff'. Save or commit per the grid's save affordance.
Review.Expectation: Both edits persist (refresh the page and the new aliases survive). The canonical name cell remains read-only in both cases. The 'baked-in' chip still shows on the SystemAdmin row.
Review.Feedback: I think that the master details may need a little work.  The Results grid is too tall.  We should use the condensed table format, provide a vertical scroll bar, and only show about 6 records in the result grid without scrolling.

Review.ItemLabel: User-type row surfaces four sub-tabs; baked-in row surfaces Mask Exemptions + privileges panel
Review.HumanAction: Select the BackofficeUser row. Inspect the details section below. Then select the CrossOrgMonitor row.
Review.Expectation: For BackofficeUser: four sub-tabs (Data Column Restrictions, Data Row Restrictions, Other UI Restrictions, Mask Exemptions). For CrossOrgMonitor: the Mask Exemptions sub-tab plus a read-only 'compiled privileges' panel showing Read-only = true and CanSeeAllOrganizations = true.

Review.ItemLabel: Add a ColumnRestriction ViewOnly for Product.UnitPrice on BackofficeUser
Review.HumanAction: With BackofficeUser selected, open Data Column Restrictions. Add a row: Table = Product, Column = UnitPrice, RestrictionKind = ViewOnly. Save.
Review.Expectation: The row persists on reload. The RestrictionKind renders as a MudToggleGroup with ViewOnly selected — no Allow option (absence of row means allowed).
Review.Feedback: The Add button is disabled.

Review.ItemLabel: Mask Exemption grant respects separation-of-duties authority rules
Review.HumanAction: While SystemAdmin, select the User baked-in row. Open the Mask Exemptions sub-tab. Try adding an exemption for Customer.SocialSecurityNumber (this assumes Session 3 seeded at least one DefaultMaskRule for SSN). Leave ExpiresAt blank.
Review.Expectation: SystemAdmin can grant the exemption without an expiry for a user-type target (the User baked-in role is user-type). Row appears with Status = Active.

Review.ItemLabel: Open feedback for Role Master Details
Review.HumanAction: Use this row for any unscripted feedback about the Role Master Details tab, the filter panel, sub-tabs, or authority-rule enforcement.

Review.ItemLabel: Default Masks grid edits and persists
Review.HumanAction: On the Default Masks tab, add a row: Table = Customer, Column = SocialSecurityNumber, MaskFormat = XXX-XX-{last4}. Save. Then use the FilterPanel to search MaskFormat contains 'last4'.
Review.Expectation: The row persists on reload. The filter reduces the grid to matching rows only. Clearing the filter restores all rows.
Review.Feedback: There is no SocialSecurityNumber listed in the Column dropdown.

Review.ItemLabel: Safety net flags undeclared sensitive-pattern columns and the Add button declares them
Review.HumanAction: Expand the 'Sensitive-name safety net' panel. Identify a flagged undeclared column (e.g., Customer.DateOfBirth). Click 'Add to Default Masks'.
Review.Expectation: The flagged column becomes a new row in the Default Masks grid with MaskFormat blank (renders as ********). The safety-net panel rescans and no longer flags that column. Saving a non-matching row does not falsely re-add flags elsewhere.
Review.Feedback: The column did get added to the list, but I had to refresh the browser to see it.

Review.ItemLabel: A new Default Mask becomes available to the Mask Exemptions sub-tab in the same circuit
Review.HumanAction: Add a new Default Mask (any Table + Column) on the Default Masks tab. Without reloading, click the Role Master Details tab, select the User row, and open the Mask Exemptions sub-tab. Attempt to add a new exemption.
Review.Expectation: The Table/Column cascading dropdowns in Mask Exemptions include the just-added column without a page reload.

Review.HumanAction: Use this row for any unscripted feedback about the Default Masks tab or the sensitive-name safety net.

Review.ItemLabel: Grid renders organizations; filter panel narrows results
Review.HumanAction: Signed in as SystemAdmin, open Organization Master Details. Use the FilterPanel to filter on Key contains 'cust-'.
Review.Expectation: The grid shows the seeded organizations (Internal Organization + one per customer). The filter narrows the list to customer-based organizations only. Clearing the filter restores the full list.
Review.Feedback: It works, but I have to use cust without the dash.

Review.ItemLabel: Create a new organization, edit its name, archive it
Review.HumanAction: Click the new-organization action. Create with Key = 'uat-test-org' and Name = 'UAT Test Org'. Save. Then reopen and change the Name to 'UAT Test Org (renamed)'. Save. Finally, archive it.
Review.Expectation: All three mutations persist across reload. The archived organization no longer appears under the default filter but is reachable with an archived-rows toggle (if provided).
Review.Feedback:
Clicking on the New Organization doesn't obviously produce a new organization, I had to scroll to the bottom.  This is another reason why some UX work on master details component sets would be helpful.  This particular use case might lean toward the vertical-layout tabs.  Clicking on a new Organization would take you to the Details tab (which could be renamed New for new records).

Otherwise, everything seems to work but you have to refresh the browser to see the added record.  The results grid should be dynamically updated to reflect new and updated records, as well as changes to the filter grid.

Review.Expectation: Five expansion panels exist for the baked-in roles (SystemAdmin, CrossOrgUserAdmin, CrossOrgMonitor, UserAdmin, User) each with canonical name, default alias, description, and a Capabilities list. Two additional panels summarize user-type default privileges and the Default Masks / Mask Exemptions semantics. CrossOrgMonitor shows 'read-only' in its Capabilities list.

Review.Expectation: The panel header shows the new display alias ('Platform Owner'), and the canonical-name line still shows SystemAdmin and the default alias. No page reload should be required.

Review.ItemLabel: Tab strip, grids, and filter panels have consistent spacing and contrast
Review.HumanAction: As SystemAdmin, cycle through all five tabs. Watch for readable text, adequate spacing between the app bar and the tab strip, readable selected-tab state, and readable baked-in-chip and greyed-row rendering.
Review.Expectation: No layout overlap. Selected-tab state is visually distinct without losing contrast. Baked-in chips remain legible on greyed rows. No elements are clipped behind the app bar.
Review.Feedback: Layout is OK.  Cannot see Users and Role Assignment.

Review.ItemLabel: Keyboard users can reach and operate every tab and grid
Review.HumanAction: Using only the keyboard, tab through the dashboard from the app bar down to a row in each tab's grid. Confirm focus is visible at every stop.
Review.Expectation: Visible focus ring on every interactive element. Tab order is logical. Arrow keys in the tab strip operate as expected. Dialogs and editors can be dismissed with Escape.
Review.Feedback: Tabbing is not that important, except for data entry. You cannot tab through the tabs, but I don't really care about that.

Review.HumanAction: Use this row for any unscripted feedback about accessibility, styling, or overall dashboard polish.

Review.Feedback:
Given that this master-details set of controls is a common idiom, it might be worth investing more in the real estate management of the set.  It might be nice to wrap the Search Results Grid in a MudExpansionPanel that when an item is selected automatically collapses and displays the selected row in the Panel header (using RenderFragment).  Changing the filter content would reset the MudExpansionPanel's header and expand the Result Grid.  That is a nice-to-have, but it would improve the UX and the result grid could show more records without scrolling (e.g., 10). 

Alternatively we might use a vertical-layout tabs control -- with a tab for the results grid and a tab for the details.  Selecting an item in the results grid navigates to the details grid.  Changing the search filters navigates to the results grid again.  That option could be OK from a UX perspective.  We might want to try both options.
As a separate note, the Tables are plural in the dropdown.  I think that the Microsoft convention is given them singular names.
I thought that we were supposed to do Playwright tests before subjecting the human to testing.  There are clearly errors in the UI that Playwright tests would have caught.

Review.Subarea: Authority rule: no SystemAdmin assignment by CrossOrgUserAdmin
Review.Feedback: See how this wastes time when you don't test this first.
Before any UAT, I think that you should perform the exact same steps in Playwright -- exact parameters so that I am not wasting my time here.
